decision: port on branch android-tutor in worktree ~/git/bp-wt/bodyhack-infinity-android, from posing-tutor c2a1b02
why: keep the web PR separate; the port builds on the tutor code

decision: install JDK 21 and the Android SDK in user space with a rerunnable script
why: no Android tools on this machine; no sudo needed; reviewers can rerun it

decision: operator: recent Pixel (Android 14+), emulator-only testing for now, coach calls this computer over Tailscale
why: facts and preferences only the operator has

decision: route both the coach and jev intent through this computer's server; phone keeps a keyword fallback
why: the jev key and omp login stay on one machine; voice commands still work offline through keywords

decision: prototype two architectures before choosing: Capacitor WebView wrapper vs native Kotlin with MediaPipe Android
why: architecture is a one-way door; reuse of the TS code vs native speed and native speech need evidence

decision: choose a Capacitor app that reuses the web tutor, with native plugins for speech, storage and keep-awake
why: the full gate passes in the WebView unchanged, so one implementation stays the truth; native needs about 2,400 domain lines plus a 3D port; speed risk is covered by a later native tracker behind tracker.ts

decision: neither emulator mode reaches the RX 7900; GPU and phone speed stay INCONCLUSIVE until the operator installs on the Pixel
why: llvmpipe and swiftshader only; GPU delegate crashed or failed in both prototypes

decision: keep photos in app-private storage on the phone; gallery export later
why: body photos are private; operator said not to worry about sharing yet

decision: operator chose Capacitor with native tracking from the start
why: operator decision at the checkpoint

decision: native plugin owns the camera and draws the preview behind a transparent WebView; landmarks use the web convention (upright, unmirrored)
why: the WebView cannot share the camera with CameraX; one landmark convention keeps metrics.ts unchanged

decision: wave 1 in parallel: platform seam (web), desktop bridge (server), Capacitor scaffold plus native pose plugin (android/)
why: the three touch disjoint files and all depend only on the committed contract

decision: desktop bridge done: Tailscale range plus bearer token for health, coach and intent only; photos stay refused
why: unit A2; curl from the Tailscale IP: 403 without token, 200 with token, photos 403 even with token; real intent and coach calls OK

decision: platform seam done; web tutor unchanged: Learn hit 99.5 to 98.5, Hold mean 98.4 to 98.5, gate PASS; a grep test forbids browser APIs in ui/ and progress/
why: unit A1; reran tsc, vitest 154 and gate myself

decision: Capacitor app and native pose plugin done: 29 fps on emulator CPU, landmarks within 3-8 px of web, detectImage elbow within 0.007 deg of web CPU, photos upright and unmirrored, GPU watchdog falls back to CPU
why: unit A3; I checked the live overlay screenshot myself

decision: allowed swangle_indirect and headless -gpu host to exercise the GPU-fail watchdog
why: swiftshader fails at GPU creation, so the watchdog path never ran; the check found and fixed a crash in closing a failed landmarker

decision: merge units A4 and A6 into one Android platform agent; give the Android gate and e2e harness (A5) to a separate agent in parallel
why: all adapters live in android.ts; a separate author for the checks keeps them independent of the code they judge

decision: add modelBase to the Platform (web: model, Android: model-lite)
why: the app bundles only the lite model; the figure asked for model/* and got 404; the seam is where device differences belong

decision: write a small native voice plugin instead of @capacitor-community/speech-recognition
why: the community plugin cannot prefer offline, has no cancel, stop never resolves, and drops errors in continuous mode

decision: Android gate feeds renders through a VIDEO-mode native detector (optional timestampMs on detectImage), not IMAGE mode
why: IMAGE mode hid the abs-and-thighs wrist (vis 0.13-0.18) and scored 100 vs desktop 93.7; the live app tracks frame to frame, so the gate must test that path

decision: emulator on swiftshader exits when WebGL and the CameraX preview run together (6 of 6); verify services with WebGL off and search for an emulator GPU mode that survives both
why: looks like an emulator graphics bug, not app logic: the probe without WebGL never crashed, and WebGL-off ran 100+ s

decision: Android harness done: android:gate PASS twice (16 poses within 4.4 points of desktop, VIDEO mode, CPU 48 ms), android:e2e 7/7 checks twice
why: unit A5

decision: Android platform done: native pose source, native TTS, native voice plugin, app-private photos, bridge pairing, keep-awake; Learn hit with photo, paired intent 1.1 s, coach 5.9 s
why: units A4 and A6; reran tsc x3 and vitest 177 myself
result: green; keep-awake and on-device photo delete not checked on device

decision: emulator runs the figure plus camera only with -gpu host (llvmpipe via DISPLAY=:0, no window); both harness scripts use it
why: swiftshader exits, swangle sends no camera frames

decision: fix negative time-to-hit at the root: a hold cannot start before its session (clamp since to startedAt in session.ts and hold.ts)
why: e2e showed 'hit in -0.3 s' when the athlete was already in the pose; affects web too

decision: turn off Android backup and device transfer (allowBackup false, dataExtractionRules exclude all)
why: Auto Backup would copy body photos and the bridge token to Google Drive; the privacy note says photos stay on the phone

decision: PhoneLayout stopped mid-run; a fresh agent finishes unit 7 from its uncommitted work
why: 5 of 6 phone checks passed; the failing check was the driver waiting for a holding phase the app had already passed (hit in 2.3 s)

decision: unit 7 verified on the emulator: phone-shots.ts 20 of 20 checks; the driver logs stage changes in the page every 50 ms and keeps a stage screenshot only if the stage outlasts the capture lag
why: the old driver polled for holding and missed a 2.3 s hold while it took a screenshot; an attached DevTools client sets KEEP_SCREEN_ON on the window, so the old keep-awake check passed without the app (control screen stayed on)
evidence: docs/android/shots/phone/results.md; KeepAwake.isKeptAwake false while dumpsys showed KEEP_SCREEN_ON with CDP attached
result: green; score 13.5% of screen height portrait, 15.8% landscape
